gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build path is the smallest honest place to make the runtime kretprobe lane visible beside atomic64, bitmap, and trace-events without widening into an unfinished starter.
A dedicated survey gate keeps the missing runtime kretprobe pilot explicit, reviewable, and tied to one Linux sample anchor instead of disappearing into generic roadmap prose.
The next real product step is a bounded starter that models probe descriptor metadata, registration lifecycle, and entry-versus-return accounting without claiming kernel-loader parity.
A focused module gate should arrive with the starter sample so lifecycle transitions, missed-instance accounting, and elapsed-time bookkeeping stay reviewable.
After the starter lands, a tiny table-driven differential gate can replay symbol-name, maxactive, and nmissed expectations from the Linux sample before any broader runtime work.
Real register_kretprobe, unregister_kretprobe, pt_regs handling, and module-init parity still depend on runtime substrate pieces that Zigux has not started yet.
